During the transition, coupled adiabatic--entropy evolution produces a localized enhancement of the curvature power spectrum. We compute the PBH abundance from this spectrum assuming Gaussian primordial curvature perturbations and using the nonlinear compaction-function formalism with a spectrum-dependent collapse threshold and critical collapse. Representative benchmark solutions yield asteroid-mass PBHs with a potentially significant dark-matter abundance, together with an associated SIGW background.

title: The Size-Mass Relation and Inside-Out Quenching of Massive Quiescent Galaxies at $2<z<3$ with JWST PRIMER and MINERVA
comment: 27 pages, 13 figures, Submitted to ApJ, Comments Welcome
summary: We investigate the morphology, size--mass relations, and spatially resolved star formation histories of 26 massive quiescent galaxies at cosmic noon ($2 < z < 3$) in the Ultra-Deep Survey field using deep JWST NIRCam imaging from the PRIMER and MINERVA surveys. Combining 16 broadband and medium-band filters with empirical point spread function matching, we perform single-Sérsic modeling and bulge--disk decompositions with pysersic across six filters (F115W to F444W), alongside Bayesian size--mass fitting with dynesty. In the rest-frame optical (F200W), the size--mass relation exhibits a steep slope of $α= 0.59 \pm 0.12$ and effective radius of $A = 0.83_{-0.07}^{+0.08}\ \mathrm{kpc}$ at $M_* = 5 \times 10^{10}\ M_\odot$. In the rest-frame near-infrared (F356W), we derive $α= 0.56 \pm 0.13$ and a more compact radius of $A = 0.70_{-0.06}^{+0.07}\ \mathrm{kpc}$. Two-thirds of the sample are bulge-dominated ($B/T \ge 0.5$), whereas one-third are disk-dominated. These results confirm inside-out quenching, consistent with dissipative gas compaction assembling the dense core, active galactic nucleus feedback halting central star formation, and the compact bulge dynamically stabilizing the surviving disk against fragmentation.

title: Umbilic Observatories
summary: We study gravitational dynamics for the simplest example of an umbilic boundary in four-dimensional general relativity --- a three-dimensional de Sitter hypersurface embedded in a four-dimensional Minkowski world. Generally speaking, an umbilic surface has the property that its induced metric is proportional to its extrinsic curvature. We consider the case of both conformal boundary conditions, as well as Dirichlet boundary conditions imposed at the timelike hypersurface. For both cases, we find that there are no linearised modes whose imaginary frequency grows with angular momentum. The conformal boundary conditions allow for a dynamical boundary degree of freedom, in addition to the bulk excitations. The umbilic property linearly decouples the boundary Weyl mode from the bulk dynamics, yielding linearly stable dynamics. In contrast, the Dirichlet problem has no boundary mode. The umbilic hypersurfaces may thus constitute an improved starting point for defining gravitational dynamics in the presence of a timelike boundary. Throughout our analysis, we draw parallels to the structure of spatial infinity for asymptotically Minkowski spacetimes and a more finite realisation thereof.

title: Global and asymptotic properties of self-gravitating nonlinear sigma models
summary: We present an analytical study of the global and asymptotic properties of static, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat solutions in general relativity and its \(D\)-dimensional generalization with multiple minimally coupled scalar fields described by a general nonlinear sigma model. Assuming a complete Riemannian target space and a non-negative scalar potential satisfying suitable growth conditions, we prove that solutions remain regular at every finite nonzero radius and can be extended inward to a naked singularity at the center. In particular, this excludes singularities on spherical shells at finite radius. We further show that all solutions exhibit universal asymptotic behavior near the central singularity. Finally, we demonstrate that these spacetimes can possess at most one photon sphere, which, if present, is necessarily unstable.

title: Two-Fluid Radial Stability of Dark-Matter-Admixed Compact Objects: Dark Compact Planets, Dark White Dwarfs, Dark Neutron Stars, and Dark Oysters
summary: We investigate the equilibrium structure and stability against radial oscillations of a variety of two-fluid compact objects containing ordinary baryonic matter admixed with cold dark matter coupled through the background spacetime. For the ordinary fluid, we employ a QCD equation of state compatible with chiral effective field theory at nuclear densities (supplemented by the BPS and Negele-Vautherin models at extremely low densities) and with perturbative QCD in the high-density regime while also satisfying also current astrophysical data. For the dark fluid, we assume self-interacting fermionic matter with particle masses of $m_f=$ 2, 5, 10, and 100 GeV and two self-interaction strengths of $y=0.1$ and $10^3$. By scanning a large range of central pressures for both fluids, we identify the presence of dark compact planets, dark white dwarfs, dark neutron stars and the so-called dark oysters. Importantly, these objects are not only in two-fluid hydrostatic equilibrium, but they are also stable against two-fluid radial oscillations. We find that the relative representation of each class in the radially stable sample is strongly sensitive to the combinations of $m_f$ and $y$, with some combinations entirely suppressing some of these object classes within the sampled domain while favoring others. In addition to these classes, strong self-repulsion supports stable, dark-matter-dominated branches with compact ordinary-matter cores and extended dark halos, approaching the self-interacting fermion-star limit. Finally, we calculate the gravitational redshift at the ordinary-matter surface, $z_{\rm OM}$, including the contribution of extended dark-matter halos for which we found radially stable configurations with $z_{\rm OM}>2$.

title: More Eccentric, Not Always Less Detectable: High Mass Holds Its Ground, Low Mass Loses Reach
summary: Gravitational waves from eccentric compact binary coalescences trace dynamical binary formation, but matched-filtering searches responsible for most detections rely on quasicircular templates. Quantifying any sensitivity loss is crucial for assessing population completeness and the need for dedicated eccentric template banks. We present the first systematic GstLAL search study spanning eccentricities up to $e_{\rm 15Hz}=0.99$ and broad ranges of chirp mass, mass ratio, inclination, and aligned spin. Using TEOBResumS-Dalí waveforms, we inject eccentric signals and measure recovered signal-to-noise ratio, signal-consistency statistics, false-alarm rate, and sensitive volume and distance. For high-mass binaries ($\mathcal{M}_c\gtrsim30\,M_\odot$), sensitive distance is nearly independent of eccentricity, demonstrating that greater eccentricity does not necessarily reduce search sensitivity. In contrast, for low-mass binaries, sensitive distance falls by up to $\sim50\%$ near $e_{\rm 15Hz}\approx0.75$. Although the absolute loss in reach is modest given their low quasicircular sensitivity, this relative reduction exceeds the increase in sensitive distance between the second and third observing runs of the LIGO--Virgo--KAGRA collaboration and is consistent with previous low-mass studies. We also find that waveform matches at fixed source parameters substantially overpredict search sensitivity loss, meaning that the pipeline's signal-consistency test and maximization over its template bank mitigate much of the predicted sensitivity loss. This highlights the need for end-to-end injection campaigns to establish the detectability of eccentric binaries.

title: Two-loop matter power spectrum from FFTLog and kite integrals
summary: We present a fast and accurate method for computing the two-loop matter power spectrum in the Effective Field Theory of Large-Scale Structure (EFTofLSS). Using FFTLog, we decompose the linear power spectrum into complex power laws, reducing the two-loop corrections to cosmology-independent massless Feynman integrals of kite topology. A central numerical challenge is the evaluation of these integrals for complex powers with large imaginary parts, where the highly oscillatory integrands make accurate numerical evaluation particularly challenging. We overcome this difficulty using a Mellin--Barnes representation summed over a uniform lattice, achieving approximately ten digit precision even for large imaginary powers, with an error estimate for each integral. The resulting precomputed matrices allow the two-loop power spectrum to be evaluated for a new cosmology in a few milliseconds. Comparing with direct numerical integration, we find agreement at the $10^{-4}$ level relative to the power spectrum up to $k=0.2$ $h$Mpc$^{-1}$ after accounting for EFTofLSS counterterm contributions and FFTLog decomposition errors. The same framework extends to biased tracers and redshift-space distortions, providing the building blocks for general two-loop calculations in EFTofLSS. We make the code for evaluating the kite integrals publicly available, together with precomputed matrices and an implementation for the two-loop matter power spectrum as a concrete application. Our results can be directly incorporated into existing FFTLog-based codes for large-scale structure, extending their current one-loop capabilities to two loops within the same computational framework.

title: Stellar Bars Reshape the Spatial Distribution of UV-bright Clumps in Nearby Galaxies
comment: 20 pages, 16 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Stellar bars redistribute gas and angular momentum in disk galaxies, but whether they mainly change the amount or the spatial organization of recent star formation remains uncertain. We use archival HST/WFC3 F275W imaging to study 70 barred galaxies and 95 unbarred control galaxies matched in stellar mass, optical color, redshift, and F275W background noise. A uniform dendrogram-based procedure identifies 95,486 UV-bright star-forming clumps. We compare their radial and azimuthal distributions, central F275W emission, and luminosity and size distribution functions. Relative to their controls, barred galaxies show a deficit of clumps at intermediate radii broadly corresponding to the bar region, followed by a local recovery near the bar ends. Their clumps are also preferentially concentrated along the bar major axis. These spatial differences are stronger in high-mass galaxies. Normalized bar length is more closely associated with the radial redistribution and central F275W concentration than bar ellipticity, although its relation to the azimuthal distribution is less uniform. When galactocentric radius is normalized by bar length, the recovery occurs near $R/R_{\rm bar}\sim1$, indicating that the bar sets a characteristic scale for the redistribution. Despite these spatial differences, barred and control galaxies have broadly similar clump luminosity and size distribution functions. Our results suggest that stellar bars mainly reorganize where recent star formation occurs, rather than substantially altering the observed luminosities and sizes of individual UV clumps, and that this effect depends on galaxy mass and bar extent.

title: All Symmetries and Boundaries of the Two-Dimensional Free Scalar from Continuous Flat-Gauging
summary: We propose a remote detectability criterion for two-dimensional conformal field theories, which asserts that any local operator outside of the product of the left- and right-moving Virasoro algebras can be detected by some topological line defect. We discuss its relationship to existing results in the conformal net literature. We then use this criterion to argue that the known $SU(2)$ moduli space of unitary conformal boundary conditions and the $SO(4)$ moduli space of unitary topological line defects of the $SU(2)_1$ Wess-Zumino-Witten model completely capture all unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological lines of the theory. Invoking the fact that the non-compact boson conformal field theory can be obtained from $SU(2)_1$ by "flat-gauging" a $U(1)$ symmetry, we are also able to completely classify the unitary conformal boundaries and unitary topological line defects of the two-dimensional free scalar field. In particular, we find a 4-dimensional moduli space of topological line defects, most of which were not known previously. We support our proposed classifications by writing down concrete Lagrangian descriptions of all of the boundaries and lines of the non-compact boson. For every boundary condition, we calculate the corresponding boundary state, and for each pair of boundary conditions, we calculate the corresponding interval Hilbert space. We verify that the annulus partition functions of the theory respect open/closed duality. We also calculate the fusion rules of the topological line defects, their action on local operators, their action on the boundary conditions by parallel fusion, and their corresponding twisted-sector Hilbert spaces.

title: Dynamics of spinning test particles in the innermost stable circular orbit of an approximate Kerr-like spacetime with mass quadrupole
summary: We study the motion of spinning test particles in a deformed, rotating spacetime described by a metric perturbed up to second order in the mass quadrupole moment. We examine how the parameters of the innermost stable circular orbit (ISCO) --namely the radius, energy, and angular momentum-- are modified by the particle's spin, contrasting our findings with both the spinless case and standard Kerr benchmarks. By employing effective potential techniques, we consider both co-rotating and counter-rotating configurations, corresponding to parallel and antiparallel alignments of the angular momenta. Using the Euler--Lagrange formalism and Hamiltonian dynamics within the Mathisson--Papapetrou--Dixon framework, we derive an explicit general ISCO equation incorporating the spin and quadrupole parameters, alongside analytical expressions for the conserved orbital quantities. Furthermore, by taking the Schwarzschild, Lense--Thirring and Kerr limits within our generalized framework, we establish new ISCO equations and compact expressions for the energy and angular momentum that extend these fundamental spacetimes to the case of spinning test particles.

title: Toward a Three-Body Holonomy Standard Model
summary:
We propose a phenomenological framework toward a Three-Body Holonomy Standard Model in which the number three is selected by the minimal primitive cyclic structure of a democratic many-body interaction network. The resulting threefold holonomy information is assumed to survive in $(3+1)$ dimensions as an internal three-state space.
  A Lorentz-invariant six-fermion interaction provides a candidate microscopic origin of the internal cyclic correlations, with their matching to Wilson holonomy left as a dynamical requirement. The parity-related holonomy sectors of the underlying $(1+1)$-dimensional Dirac system motivate left- and right-handed internal structures and a trinification-like $SU(3)_C\times SU(3)_L\times SU(3)_R$ gauge completion.
  Vertical holonomy selects a $2+1$ splitting, while spontaneous left-right vacuum misalignment provides a possible route to chiral symmetry breaking. Horizontal holonomy organizes the three-family mass structure, with heavy-fermion mixing generating effective flavor and CP-violating patterns.
  Although a complete ultraviolet derivation remains open, the framework provides a unified scenario connecting primitive three-body dynamics to gauge symmetry, symmetry breaking, and fermion flavor.

title: The Effect of Large Apertures on Atmospheric Noise Spectra for Millimeter-wave Telescopes
summary: Ground-based millimeter and submillimeter telescopes produce astronomical maps that contain a combination of noise inherent to themselves as well as contamination from foregrounds, with the strongest foreground being fluctuating atmospheric emission. While the emission of the turbulent atmosphere itself follows a scale-free power law, the atmosphere as seen by the telescope is modified by the properties of the instrument optics. A naive power-law extrapolation of the atmospheric noise spectrum ignores the blurring effect of the near-field beam, which becomes more pronounced for larger telescope apertures and at higher multipoles. In this work, we use a toy model to derive a semianalytic estimate of the atmospheric noise spectrum that takes into account the effects of near-field optics. We show that it has an appreciable effect for large-aperture telescopes, suggesting that ultra-sensitive, high-resolution experiments are not necessarily limited by the atmosphere on small angular scales. We also present an estimate of the atmospheric knee as a function of the primary aperture, the atmospheric scale height, and the outer scale of turbulence.

title: Cosmology with post-EoR 21 cm Intensity Mapping surveys: power spectrum measurements in the last decade
comment: 32 pages, 3 figures, review submitted to Universe (MDPI)
summary: The technique of 21 cm intensity mapping (IM) is emerging as a possible, cost-effective method to supplement optical surveys to map the large-scale structure, and extend their redshift reach, with projects aiming to cover a large range of post-EoR redshifts, from z=0 to z=6. Since the early discussions 20 years ago, a few dedicated interferometers have been built, and surveys have been carried out using them as well as general purpose radio instruments. An introduction to late-time cosmology with 21 cm intensity mapping is given, highlighting the main scientific and technical challenges. We present then an overview of different instrument concepts and survey strategies, followed by a discussion of outstanding data analysis challenges, most notably the foreground subtraction, which is a major issue in IM. We carry on with a presentation of the currently active projects and the 21 cm signal measurements which have been obtained, either in cross-correlation with optical surveys, or as the autocorrelation power spectrum. Finally, we discuss briefly the prospects for this field with future instruments and surveys such as SKA, HIRAX and CHORD.

title: Kinematic Map of the Galactic Bulge Using HST Proper Motions
comment: 14 pages, 9 figures, 1 table; submitted to MNRAS
summary: Constraining the Galactic bulge's non-axisymmetric dynamics requires proper motions in deep fields across many sightlines, yet crowding and extinction limit such measurements. Using multi-epoch observations of 27 fields in the southern Galactic bulge (-6$^\circ$ < l < 4$^\circ$, -5$^\circ$ < b < -1$^\circ$) from the ultraviolet-visible (UVIS) channel of Wide Field Camera 3 (WFC3) on the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) with time baselines of 3 to 13 years, and combining them with the absolute proper motion reference frame provided by Gaia Data Release 3 (DR3), we measure absolute proper motions for ~ 400,000 stars. Colour-magnitude diagrams are used to separate bulge stars from foreground disc stars, identify red clump stars and correct for interstellar extinction and reddening. Statistical analysis shows that the mean proper motion in Galactic latitude is consistent with that of the central supermassive black hole Sgr A*, while the mean proper motion in Galactic longitude is affected by disc stars but agrees with Sgr A* after extrapolation to the Galactic plane. Proper motion dispersions increase towards the Galactic centre and are asymmetric across Galactic longitude, with a steeper gradient for l < 0$^\circ$, revealing the bulge's non-axisymmetric bar structure. The velocity distribution shows clear anisotropy ($σ_l$/$σ_b$ = 1.131 $\pm$ 0.005). The normalised covariance is negative in the l > 0$^\circ$ region (~ -0.085) and close to zero in the l < 0$^\circ$ region. The proper motion distributions are non-Gaussian in both Galactic longitude and latitude, mainly due to contamination by foreground disc stars.

title: Proof of the entropic $c$-theorem
summary: We prove an entropic $c$-theorem in two dimensions by constructing a $c$-function from the mutual information between spacelike separated wedges, defined through the relative entropy. The proof follows Casini and Huerta's, with strong subadditivity of entanglement entropy replaced by increasing differences of the mutual information, which we prove directly in the continuum from the split property and standard properties of relative entropy. The benefit of relative entropy is that every quantity we use is finite and no cutoff ever needs to be introduced. The assumptions of the theorem are only the standard axioms of algebraic quantum field theory, the split property with finite mutual information across a gap (both implied by modular $p$-nuclearity), and a finite ultraviolet bound on the resulting $c$-functions. We also note that, formally, the $c$-function is proportional to the minimal averaged null energy of a state that reproduces the vacuum correlations between the two wedges.

title: Nonthermal coalescence parameter of light nuclei production in pp collisions at LHC energies
summary: We study the light nucleus production in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}=7$ and $13$~TeV reported by the ALICE Collaboration within the color string fragmentation framework. We adopt the Schwinger mechanism with string tension fluctuations as the particle production mechanism describing the $p_T$ spectrum. The approximately thermal behavior observed in the light-nucleus spectra motivates the use of a perturbative series expansion of the $q$-Gaussian string tension fluctuations around $q=1$. The resulting $p_T$ spectrum is expressed as a perturbative series expansion around the thermal distribution with nonthermal corrections given by Gamma distributions, providing closed forms for the effective temperature, moments, and cumulants. In the superstatistical framework, the associated temperature fluctuations show that the medium in which light nuclei are produced is out of equilibrium. Additionally, we derive closed formulas for the coalescence parameter at arbitrary order, which agree well with experimental data. Our results also show that the mass--temperature relation ($T_N/m_N \approx AT_A/m_A$) between the nucleons and nuclei is not preserved in the coalescence process.

title: Elastic boundaries in Stochastic Inflation
summary: In the context of stochastic inflation, specifying boundary conditions is often a requirement to distinguish domains where quantum diffusion takes place from regions where stochastic effects are suppressed compared to the standard slow-roll evolution. Yet, even though the transition between the two is expected to be smooth and continuous, most of the literature has hitherto focused on absorbing and reflective boundaries. We consider here the use of a broader class of boundaries, called elastic, which involves one free parameter interpolating between these two limiting cases. We show how the conventional stochastic-$δN$, and its recently proposed time-reversed counterpart adapt to such a class of boundary behaviour. As an illustration, we solve time-reversed stochastic inflation for an exactly flat semi-infinite potential with an elastic boundary, a setup where the standard stochastic-$δN$ formalism breaks down, and compare the results to the purely absorbing case. Quantitative differences are found in terms of skewness and tail behaviour. This suggests that the transition between stochastic inflation and subsequent evolution may have observable consequences. Finally, we show that an elastic boundary stands as an effective model for stochastic tunnelling through a Dirac delta potential barrier. This mechanism can be equivalently framed as a smooth transition of stochastic trajectories in a mirror virtual medium with specific absorption properties.

title: Resolving the Complex Line-Locking Structure in Quasar J004613+010425 with VLT/X-shooter Spectroscopy
comment: 15 pages, 10 figures, 2 tables; accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Line-locking (LL) signatures in quasar absorption-line systems provide direct observational evidence for radiatively driven outflows. We present a detailed investigation of LL phenomena in the quasar SDSS J004613.54+010425.7 ($z_{\rm em} = 2.150$) using medium-resolution VLT/X-shooter spectra, as part of the TOLL project. Compared with previous studies based on Sloan Digital Sky Survey spectroscopy, the X-shooter data resolve the absorption complex into twelve narrow absorption line (NAL) components spanning $\sim$$2700$ km/s in the C IV, N V, Si IV, and Ly$α$ transitions, a factor of $\sim$2.4 more components than identified from lower resolution spectra. We detect fourteen distinct LL pairs across three ionic species, forming one of the largest line-locking webs known to date: three Si IV pairs connecting components (2, 10), (4, 11), and (5, 12); six N V pairs organized into four groups; and five C IV pairs organized into three groups. Monte Carlo simulations show that the probability of this twelve-component LL web arising by chance is $< 10^{-5}$. Photoionization modeling with Cloudy yields ionization parameters of $\log U \approx -2.4$ to $-0.6$ and total hydrogen column densities of $\log N({\rm H}) \approx 18.4$-$20.6$ for the twelve components. A comparison of the properties of shadowed and shadowing clouds shows that ion column densities and ionization parameters typically agree within a factor of $\sim$3, broadly supporting the standard radiative acceleration picture, although several outliers suggest that multi-ion locking and cloud-cloud interactions may also regulate LL stability. These results demonstrate that medium- and high-resolution spectroscopy is essential for resolving the full complexity of line-locked quasar outflows.

title: Hilbert space in the flat limit of AdS/CFT. II. Massless particles
summary: Building on Part I of this series, where we described the emergence of massive scattering states, we demonstrate how unitary lowest-weight representations $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ of the conformal group with fixed dimension $Δ$ and arbitrary integer spin $s$ contract to massless Poincaré particle representations. This requires combining the Inönü--Wigner contraction $\mathfrak{so}(2,3) \to \mathfrak{iso}(1,3)$ with an infinite boost, in which case massless scattering states naturally emerge in a carrollian basis. For $Δ>s+1$, we find that $\mathcal D(Δ,s)$ contracts to the direct sum of massless particles of all spins $s'\leq s$. At the unitarity bound, lower-spin states become null so that $\mathcal D(s+1,s)$ contracts to a single massless particle representation carrying the two maximal helicities $J=\pm s$. In both cases, the inner product converges to the Poincaré-invariant one after a single helicity-independent rescaling, so that unitarity is preserved throughout the contraction.

title: Probing dark sector with decihertz gravitational wave observations of compact binary inspirals in IndIGO-D
summary: We investigate the potential of decihertz gravitational-wave (GW) observations of compact-binary inspirals to probe atomic dark matter (aDM) and its interactions through an ultralight massive dark photon. We consider a scenario in which neutron stars accumulate DM charged under a dark Abelian massive vector mediator, leading to an additional long-range Yukawa interaction between compact objects and associated dipolar radiation. In this framework, the GW waveform acquires characteristic corrections parameterized by the Yukawa coupling strength $α$, the dipole-radiation parameter $γ$, and a parameter related to the mediator mass $μ$. These corrections include a leading $-1$ post-Newtonian dipole contribution and finite-mediator-mass effects. We relate the aDM corrections to existing parameterized tests of general relativity and perform Bayesian parameter-estimation analyses for simulated binary neutron star (BNS) and neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems incorporating the modified binary inspiral in a proposed space-based decihertz detector, named IndIGO-D. For a GW170817-like BNS with nonzero aDM couplings chosen near current observational bounds, we find that the dark-photon rest energy can be inferred with a $90\%$ credible uncertainty of $O(10^{-20})\,\mathrm{eV}$, conditional on a detectable dark-sector contribution. Analyses with weaker dark-sector interactions $(α\lesssim O(10^{-8}))$ show that the mediator mass remains unconstrained when both the Yukawa coupling and dipole-radiation contribution are negligible, but can be measured even for a negligible Yukawa coupling if the dipole-radiation contribution is sufficiently strong. Our results demonstrate that future decihertz GW observatories can serve as powerful laboratories for testing dark-sector physics and probing dark matter interactions in compact binaries through precision GW measurements.

title: Updated $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures
summary: In order to study the new $Σ_{c}$ baryons observed by the LHCb collaboration recently, we update the previously predicted $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum by extending the excited states up to the highly excited $2P$- and $1F$-wave states. The calculation is performed in the framework of the relativized quark model and Gaussian expansion method by considering the mixing effect. The radially and orbitally excited states in the calculation are determined by the truncation convention proposed in this work and the mechanism of the heavy-quark dominance. The contribution of each Hamiltonian term to the energy levels is precisely calculated by using the two-step Gaussian expansion method. Then, the concerned $Σ_{c}$ states are obtained and the $Σ_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures is established. Based on these, several important topics are discussed and analyzed, including the root-mean-square radii, off-diagonal matrix elements, mixing effect, fine structures and assignments of the newly observed $Σ_{c}(2800)^{0}$, $Σ_{c}(2900)^{0}$ and $Σ_{c}(3200)^{0}$ states. Meanwhile, it is found that the approximate decoupling phenomenon emerges in different $nL$-wave groups. This implies the reasonability of the truncation convention and is of great significance for further improving the calculation scheme for all the baryon spectra. Moreover, it is demonstrated that in the very high-lying $nL$-wave groups such as the $1F$-wave group, the energy level gaps become small even degenerate, and each of the baryon states has a big radius and therefore a loosely bound structure. In addition, by examining the experimental and calculated data, we suggest more precise experiments to search for more $Σ_{c}$ baryon states in the predicted $1P$- and $2P$-wave fine structures whose central energies are around 2822 and 3210 MeV, respectively.

title: Tests of equivalence principle violation in doubly coupled dark energy
comment: 22 pages, 2 figures. Submitted to Phys.Rev.D. Comments welcome!
summary: Recent work has shown that a simple form of coupled dark energy with a constant coupling produces a good fit to the DESI data. In this scenario, dark matter, but not baryons, couples to a scalar field, thereby violating the weak equivalence principle (EP). We first generalize the coupled dark energy model by adding a nonminimal coupling between the scalar field and gravity, and dub the resulting model "doubly coupled dark energy". We then construct a parameter $E_P$ in this model that quantifies EP violation on cosmological scales and can be measured with large galaxy surveys in a model-independent way. Finally, we forecast constraints on the couplings for present and future spectroscopic galaxy surveys, namely DESI, Euclid, and SKA Phase 2 (SKA2). To keep the analysis as general as possible, we leave the initial power spectrum shape and the galaxy bias free to vary in several bins. Among these surveys, SKA2 could provide the tightest constraint on the coupling strength in the coupled dark energy scenario, with a relative $1σ$ uncertainty of $22\%$. The constraints weaken when both couplings are varied, but can be further improved by increasing the number of galaxies detected.

title: OASIS I: Spectroscopy of Mini-Quenched and Lulling Galaxies Constrains the Quiet Side of Bursty Star Formation at z > 4
comment: 25 pages, 20 figures, 2 tables. Submitted to A&A. Paper I of the OASIS series; companion Papers II and III submitted simultaneously
summary: JWST has revealed that star formation in early galaxies is bursty, including episodes of violent suppression, so-called mini-quenching. But these were largely serendipitous discoveries in samples of UV-bright, emission-line-dominated galaxies, so that the quiet side of the burst cycle has remained poorly explored. With the JWST Cycle 3 program OASIS (GO 5997), we searched for such galaxies deliberately, using deep 28-hour NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy across the full burst cycle at z>4. We identify three mini-quenched galaxies with log(M*/Msun) = 8.3-8.9 and no detectable Balmer emission, at least 1.2-1.7 dex below the star-forming main sequence (SFMS), five lulling galaxies with weak Balmer emission above the quenching threshold, and 17 nearly-main-sequence galaxies just below the SFMS. Finding them required spectroscopy: seven of our ten photometric candidates for suppressed (mini-quenched and lulling) galaxies turned out to be nearly-MS or above the SFMS, and photometric fits overestimate their current star-formation rates and cannot distinguish lulling from mini-quenched ones. The suppressed galaxies are common: five of the eight come from tiers not selected on star-formation state, where they make up 29% of the galaxies at z = 4-5.5 and log(M*/Msun) = 8-9.5, a number density of ~1.6x10^-3 Mpc^-3 dex^-1. Simulations predict them to be an order of magnitude rarer at these masses and to occur mainly at lower masses. The suppressed galaxies are also old: Balmer-break strength and stellar age both increase as galaxies fall further below the SFMS, with light-weighted ages of 5 Myr for galaxies above it, ~30 Myr for the lulling galaxies and above 100 Myr for the mini-quenched ones. They show little stellar reddening (E(B-V) < 0.2), consistent with depleted gas reservoirs. Suppressed phases at z>4 are therefore neither rare nor brief, but a common and lasting part of early galaxy growth.

title: Facets of Gravity: A journey exploring spacetime from Planckian to cosmological scales
comment: 396 pages, 68 figures, 13 chapters, 7 appendices. Extended version of the doctoral thesis, including an additional part on lattice quantum affine gravity that was added after the original manuscript assessment
summary:
What does it mean to quantize gravity, and what can a quantum theory of spacetime actually predict? This thesis explores these questions through complementary non-perturbative approaches, from the geometry of quantum spacetime to the emergence of cosmological physics.
  Within Causal Dynamical Triangulations, we develop observables to investigate effective topology, statistical homogeneity, and curvature in strongly fluctuating geometries, where conventional differential-geometric tools are unavailable. Tests in two-dimensional models reveal distinct coarse-graining behaviours and provide new ways to probe the emergence of familiar geometric properties.
  We then turn to the Functional Renormalization Group and Asymptotic Safety, developing flow invariants to characterize ultraviolet-critical surfaces and introducing Flow Invariant Neural Networks as a computational method for reconstructing them. In scalar-tensor gravity, we investigate how ultraviolet consistency conditions can constrain infrared interactions, obtaining an inflationary scenario compatible with cosmological observations.
  Finally, we question whether the metric must be the fundamental variable of quantum gravity. We formulate a lattice statistical approach to purely affine gravity, in which the connection is fundamental and the metric, when it exists, is emergent. Monte Carlo simulations provide exploratory results in two dimensions, while a four-dimensional homogeneous and isotropic construction yields preliminary evidence for de Sitter-like geometry and allows the study of curvature correlations.
  Together, these investigations develop complementary tools for studying quantum spacetime, testing its possible continuum behaviour, and connecting fundamental gravitational theories with observable physics, while identifying the conceptual and computational challenges that remain.

title: Probing Realistic Neutron Star Equations of State via the Chameleon Mechanism
summary: We investigate the impact of the Chameleon mechanism on structural properties of neutron stars adopting realistic nucleonic equations of state. The scalar-matter coupling parameter $β$ controls the departure from the corresponding general-relativistic configurations, affecting both the maximum mass and the stellar radius. Our numerical results demonstrate that the chameleon mechanism can have a significant impact on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars, even when realistic equations of state are employed. Moreover, well established constraints on masses and radii of neutron stars put stringent limits on the allowed numerical values of the coupling.

title: Quantum Popcorn: the shape of a phase transition bubble
summary: A quantum tunneling event in field theory is usually depicted as the materialization of a spherical bubble of true vacuum. The bubble appears at rest, and its profile is the time-symmetric slice of Coleman's bounce, the Euclidean solution that controls the decay rate. However, the bubble is spherical only in the leading semiclassical approximation: at the next order the configuration is a Gaussian ensemble of fluctuations around the bounce. We derive the wave functional of the field on the nucleation slice from the half-bounce path integral, and use it to compute the root-mean-square quadrupole moment of a bubble at nucleation. The relative deformation of the bubble wall radius $R$ is $δR/R\sim(\hbar/S_b)^{1/2}$, with $S_b$ the bounce action. Thus $δR/R\sim0.1$ for a typical cosmological phase transition with $S_b/\hbar\sim100$.

title: Model-Independent Assessments of Tidal Alignment and Density-Weighting Dependence in Galaxy Intrinsic Alignments
summary: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxies are an important source of systematic uncertainty in weak gravitational lensing measurements and also serve as a test for models of galaxy formation and evolution. These galaxy alignments are usually modeled assuming that the IA are sourced by the tidal fields around the galaxies. However, galaxy properties, like their proximity to other galaxies and their mass, provide alignment contributions beyond the tidal field. In this work, we perform novel model-agnostic tests to determine the impact of density-weighting on the IA of galaxies using data from the IllustrisTNG cosmological hydrodynamical simulation and SDSS-III (BOSS). We show that the primary effect of density-weighting is an increase of the alignment amplitude at large scales, whereas the small-scale impact is sample-dependent. We also assess the tidal alignment paradigm for IllustrisTNG galaxies using two-point correlation functions of galaxy shapes, tidal fields, and the sampled background tidal field of the simulation box. We find, given the precision of our measurements, that central galaxies align linearly to the underlying (non-linear) tidal field well into the 1-halo regime.

title: OASIS II: The Ionized Gas Traces Feedback-Driven Declines into the Quiet Side of Bursty Star Formation at z > 4
comment: 18 pages, 10 figures, 1 table. Submitted to A&A. Paper II of the OASIS series; companion Papers I and III submitted simultaneously
summary: Models of bursty star formation in low-mass (10^8-10^9.5 Msun) galaxies at z>4 differ most in the suppressed phases: what drives the decline, how fast star formation falls, and how long it stays low. OASIS Paper I showed that such quiet galaxies are common and old; here we measure how they got there and how their ionized gas responds. We compare Balmer-line star-formation rates (SFRs) with 100-Myr averages from the stellar continuum, in NIRSpec/PRISM spectra of 54 OASIS galaxies at z>4, including three mini-quenched galaxies below the quenching threshold and five lulling galaxies at least 0.6 dex below the star-forming main sequence (SFMS) but still star-forming. Galaxies above the SFMS rise and fade equally often, whereas those below it are mostly fading: the lulling galaxies formed little more than a tenth of their mass in the last 100 Myr, and their decline began tens to ~100 Myr before observation. Suppressed phases thus last of order 100 Myr, as long as or longer than in most simulations, whereas recovery is much faster: few galaxies below the SFMS are rising. The ionized gas tracks these changes in star formation. [OIII]/[OII] falls from galaxies above the SFMS to the lulling ones, even at fixed mass and after dust correction, and follows the recent change in SFR (SFR_10/SFR_100) more closely than the position relative to the SFMS: two rising galaxies below the SFMS are highly ionized. This is expected if fewer and softer ionizing photons than in strongly star-forming galaxies meet gas depleted by earlier star formation. Lulling galaxies show ISM conditions distinct from those of strongly star-forming galaxies. The declines are faster than passive gas exhaustion predicts, favoring feedback that expels the gas or keeps it from forming stars. Quiet phases are thus long, feedback-driven episodes, and the ionized gas traces where a galaxy is in its burst cycle.

title: $h/2e$ Flux Trapping without Superconductivity
summary: Recently, it was shown by Komargodski and Popov [arXiv:2601.09847] that ordinary metals threaded with an Aharonov-Bohm solenoid exclusively trap either 0 or h/2e flux. The latter value is familiar in the superconducting setting, yet we find that it holds in ordinary metals as well, with no condensate or pairing necessary. We provide an analytic explanation for the flux trapping, and extend the results to the cases of finite temperature, time-reversal invariant potentials, and lattice regularization, where we find that the flux remains trapped at 0 and h/2e.

title: Novel thermodynamic topological subclass from inverse-temperature asymptotics
summary: We investigate the thermodynamic topology of the charged McGuigan--Nappi--Yost black hole in the canonical ensemble at fixed electric charge, identifying equilibrium black hole solutions as zeros of the thermodynamic vector field constructed from the generalized off-shell free energy. The inverse Hawking temperature diverges as the extremal limit is approached and approaches a finite positive value in the large-horizon limit. The zero points of the thermodynamic vector field reveal a thermodynamic phase structure consisting solely of a locally stable branch with positive winding number ($w=+1$). The innermost small black hole state is locally stable in the low-temperature limit. As the temperature increases, the stable branch extends toward the outermost large black hole regime, while no black hole states exist in the high-temperature regime beyond the finite upper Hawking temperature. This distinct asymptotic behavior of the inverse temperature places the thermodynamic defect structure outside the established topological (sub)classes, although its topological number agrees with that of the standard $W^{1+}$ class. We therefore identify this defect structure as a new thermodynamic topological subclass, $\breve W^{1+}$. This finding extends the existing classification to include a finite, nonzero large-horizon limit of the inverse Hawking temperature and suggests that distinct asymptotic behaviors in other black hole families may reveal further topological (sub)classes and thermodynamic phase structures.

title: Hadronic Molecules: Theory
comment: 11 pages, 3 Figures, Invited talk presented at MESON2026, Cracow, June 2026
summary: Since the turn of the century it becomes evident that the naive quark model is not capable to describe the rich phenomenology of hadrons, especially in the doubly heavy sector. For a large number of those states a molecular structure appears to be a natural description. In these proceedings I review the theory of hadronic molecules, how they can be described systematically in effective field theories and what imprint this structure leaves in observables. On two examples I explain non-trivial predictions emerging from the molecular hypothesis that can be tested in future experiments and lattice QCD calculations, promising deep insights into the inner workings of QCD.

title: OASIS III: Bursty star formation drives observed galaxy sizes at $z\geq4$
comment: 18 pages, 14 figures, 1 table. Submitted to A&A
summary: We employ JWST/NIRSpec MSA PRISM spectroscopy together with NIRCam imaging to investigate the impact of star-formation variability on galaxy sizes for a representative sample of 51 galaxies at $z\geq4$. The OASIS survey enables us to probe low-star-formation-rate (SFR) lulling and mini-quenched galaxies down to $\log_{10}(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.3$ and $\log_{10}(\mathrm{SFR}/M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1})<-1.6$, i.e. more than one order of magnitude below the star-forming main sequence (MS). This enables us to probe objects that are often missed by shallower spectroscopic surveys, in addition to the MS and starburst systems, yielding an SFR- and mass-representative sample at high redshift. We derive galaxy half-light sizes using ForcePho, enabling us to resolve the highly compact nature of these sources, and we analyse their star-formation histories and interstellar medium (ISM) properties with the full-spectral-fitting code ppxf. We find a clear anti-correlation between burstiness, as traced by the ratio of the SFR from H$α$ compared to that from non-parametric spectral fitting averaged over 100 Myr, and galaxy UV/optical half-light radii as measured with ForcePho from a combination of well-sampled NIRCam photometry. Using partial correlation coefficients we show that the anti-correlation between burstiness (as traced by the SFR ratio) and size cannot simply be explained by secondary dependencies on stellar mass or redshift. We interpret this relation as the effect of central starbursts in SFR-rising (bursting) systems, where intense central star formation reduces measured galaxy half-light sizes. This burstiness then regulates galaxy sizes at high redshift. Should the same mechanism be present at $z>10$, this could explain the size bimodality seen in the UV luminous galaxies as simply stemming from a more fundamental relationship between burstiness and size.

title: Induced Lorentzian geometry from the fermionic quantum metric
summary: Quantum geometry is conventionally understood in parameter or momentum space and need not be related to a geometry in configuration space. Here we show for Dirac fermions in a background electromagnetic field that an induced Lorentzian geometry is generated from the fermionic quantum metric. We study a Lorentz covariant phase space worldline path integral construction, whose application of the adiabatic theorem onto spin degrees of freedom leads to the appearance of the Berry phase at $O(\hbar)$, and the quantum metric at $O(\hbar^2)$ in the worldline action. Both the Feynman and retarded/advanced propagators are examined in 3+1 and 2+1 dimensions, whose different on-shell implementations lead to related quantum metrics; QED/QED${}_3$ and condensed matter Dirac theory are considered. An effective theory is found by integrating out the momenta degrees of freedom, which gives rise to an emergent Lorentzian metric in configuration space, whose perturbation to the flat metric is dependent on the quantum metric and the background field strength. Apart from the spin degrees of freedom encoded into the Berry phase, the effective theory describes a scalar particle moving in the induced quantum geometry. Phenomenological applications to the covariant geometry are further studied using spectral holonomy in a gapped 3-dimensional Dirac material.

title: Homogeneous Spectral Freedom and Hadamard Consistency of Perturbative Green Functions
comment: Dedicated to the memory of Jan Kříž. 24 pages, 2 tables
summary: Perturbative mode equations often admit formally different particular solutions whose spectral sums appear to have different short-distance singularities. We formulate a general diagnostic which separates this representational freedom from a genuine change of quantum state: for a fixed normally hyperbolic operator, two Hadamard two-point functions can differ only by a smooth homogeneous bisolution. Thus, a nonsmooth term generated by rearranging a perturbative source must be traced either to a changed operator or to inadmissible homogeneous spectral data. We apply the criterion to two impulsive plane-wave backgrounds. Starting directly from the metrics, we recompute the wave operators, modes, world functions, and Van Vleck determinants. Exact-mode matching and the geometrical construction agree through second order for the first profile. In the second, correcting the metric changes the leading perturbation from quadratic to linear order in the wave parameter and eliminates inverse transverse-momentum poles, while the corrected metric retains an exact aligned null-radiation Einstein source. In both examples the singular Green function is precisely the perturbative expansion of the Hadamard parametrix; the additional logarithms arise from momentum-singular homogeneous data. For the exactly soluble first profile, the standard flat-normalized plane-wave prescription gives a vanishing renormalized stress tensor away from the impulsive surface. Smooth-front regularizations of both profiles reproduce, at the calculated orders and away from the characteristic zero mode, the singular structure of the matched impulsive propagators without generating inverse transverse-momentum poles.

title: Phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices in the oscillating axion background
summary: We investigate the effect of an oscillating axion background on thermally induced vortex-antivortex production in the Abelian-Higgs model. Through its coupling to the gauge field, the axion sources an electromagnetic response in the presence of vortex magnetic flux, modifying the dynamics of the vortices. We study this system using Langevin lattice simulations with dissipation and stochastic noise. It is shown that the phase transition dynamics of Abelian-Higgs vortices, namely the pair creation of vortex and antivortex under thermal fluctuations, can be significantly modified in the oscillating axion background. We find that the axion background shifts the rapid increase in the vortex density to lower temperature. In particular, this transition temperature becomes smaller as the oscillation frequency of the axion increases. The temperature dependence of the correlation length is also modified. These features provide a new experimental approach for the axion dark matter using superconducting devices.

title: Leaking Sound Waves: Gravitational Waves From Dark Sectors Weakly Coupled to the Standard Model
summary: First-order phase transitions in a dark sector can produce an observable stochastic gravitational-wave background, and many models predicting such signals in current and future experiments have been explored. For moderately strong transitions, hydrodynamical simulations suggest that sound waves generated by the expansion and collisions of true-vacuum bubbles are the dominant source of gravitational waves. It is often assumed that these sound waves propagate only within the dark-sector fluid, while the impact of the visible sector is neglected. In this paper, we investigate the effects of a weak coupling between the dark and visible fluids on the resulting gravitational-wave signal. We adopt a phenomenological hydrodynamical description of two ultra-relativistic fluids, parametrizing their interactions without specifying an underlying microscopic model. We focus on the regime in which the coupling can be neglected during the phase transition but becomes relevant during the subsequent, longer-lasting period of sound wave propagation. Within this framework, we analytically show that, even if the bubble expansion initially affects only the dark fluid, sound waves can subsequently be induced in the visible sector. Using the sound-shell model, we find that, despite the additional sound waves generated in the visible sector, the total gravitational-wave signal sourced by both fluids is generally suppressed compared to the case of a completely decoupled dark sector. This suppression becomes more pronounced for larger interaction rates and a larger ratio of relativistic degrees of freedom in the visible sector to those in the dark sector. The coupling also modifies the shape of the gravitational-wave spectrum.

title: As a matter of reconstruction -- varying the magnetic Prandtl number in implicit large eddy simulations
summary: The magnetic Prandtl number ($\mathrm{Pm}$), the ratio of viscosity to magnetic diffusivity, spans many orders of magnitude in astrophysical plasmas. It shapes how turbulence amplifies and structures magnetic fields. In direct numerical simulations (DNS) the viscosity and magnetic diffusivity can be controlled explicitly and independently, whereas in implicit large eddy simulations (ILES) they are set by the numerical scheme. We test whether, in a finite-volume code, $\mathrm{Pm}$ can be varied through the reconstruction scheme by applying different methods to the hydro and magnetic variables. As a proof of concept, we simulate driven, subsonic, homogeneous magnetohydrodynamic turbulence using five pairs of hydrodynamic and magnetic reconstruction schemes at varying resolutions. We measure the effective viscosity and resistivity from the energy transfer between scales. Reconstructing the magnetic field at higher order than the fluid raises the effective magnetic Prandtl number and vice versa. We demonstrate that a mix of second- and third-order reconstruction alone results in a $\gtrsim20\times$ change in $\mathrm{Pm}$. A comparison of DNS with matched explicit dissipation at these values agrees with the ILES. Mixed reconstruction thus offers a simple and efficient way to explore $\mathrm{Pm} \not\simeq 1$ in ILES without adding explicit dissipation.

title: Reconstructing Meson Parton Distributions from Mellin Moments with Artificial Neural Networks
summary: We address the inverse problem of reconstructing a meson parton distribution function (PDF) or parton distribution amplitude (PDA) at a fixed scale from a finite set of Mellin moments. At finite moment order this map is ill posed in the Hadamard sense: the moments do not determine a unique, stable pointwise $x$-dependence, and small data perturbations can produce large changes in the reconstruction. We regularize the problem by restricting the admissible function class through constraints justified by first principles---support on $x\in[0,1]$, endpoint vanishing, unit normalization, and, for the pion, the exact $x\leftrightarrow 1-x$ symmetry---and by complementing these hard constraints with differentiable penalties that suppress the spurious multiple maxima and central concavity changes typical of ill-posed inversions. We parameterize the unknown function with two interchangeable neural cores, a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and a Kolmogorov--Arnold network (KAN), and find that the KAN reconstructs the target distributions more accurately, most markedly in the asymmetric (kaon) case. We attribute this advantage to the locality of the B-spline basis underlying the KAN, which localizes corrections during moment matching and damps the global oscillations to which the MLP is prone. Benchmarks against synthetic targets, using both ten and five input moments, support these conclusions.

title: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
summary: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. We extend this framework towards thermocosmology by introducing a running non-conservation scale $L_2(H)$, while restricting non-conservation to cold dark matter. We investigate two prescriptions, namely a Hubble-proportional rate and an inverse-Hubble running model, deriving their cosmological dynamics and effective geometric dark-energy description. The first admits an exact analytical solution and is related to quadratic running-vacuum cosmologies, while the second approaches standard matter dilution at early times and allows reversals in the direction of energy exchange. Interestingly, the reconstructed geometric dark energy can exhibit quintessence-like and phantom-like behavior, including smooth crossings of the phantom divide, without introducing a phantom field or superacceleration. A unified dynamical-system analysis reveals distinct matter-era critical configurations and a continuous family of de Sitter solutions that are transversely attracting under suitable conditions. Confronting both models with Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, we find a mild preference for positive present-day matter non-conservation. The Akaike information criterion slightly favors the thermogravity scenarios, whereas the Bayesian information criterion favors the simpler $Λ$CDM model. Thus, running thermocosmology provides a viable framework for nontrivial effective dark-energy dynamics.

title: Numerical evaluation of one-loop integrals using quadrature rules
summary: We introduce a numerical quadrature algorithm with stretched exponential convergence to evaluate one-loop integrals in dimensional regularisation in the causal Loop Tree Dual (cLTD) representation. The key feature that makes this possible is the fact that for Euclidean kinematics all singularities of the cLTD integrand lie on a compact set in loop momentum space. We prove that our algorithm admits a stretched exponential convergence with the number of integrand evaluations, and we illustrate it by evaluating triangle, box and pentagon integrals at selected Euclidean kinematics points. We benchmark our implementation against analytic results as well as results obtained via Monte Carlo integration. We also provide a proof of concept that our algorithm can be extended to physical kinematics after subtraction of threshold singularities.

title: OASIS III: Bursty star formation drives observed galaxy sizes at $z\geq4$

title: Dark Halos, Intermediate-Mass BH and Nuclear Stellar Clusters in Dwarf Spheroidals
summary: We exploit the halo densities of three dwarf spheroidals recently obtained to investigate their dark matter distribution. We address the well-known DM halo core-cusp issue by finding that the NFW $Λ$CDM halo profile is in strong disagreement with these inferred halo densities, which instead result very well-reproduced by the Burkert halo cored profile with the central density $ρ_0$ and the core radius $r_0$. These structural parameters result connected among themselves and with the length scale of the stellar matter component in a way similar to that present in disk systems. By analyzing the properties of dark halo densities in their innermost regions, we find no trace of a central intermediate-mass black hole or of a nuclear stellar cluster.

title: Longitudinal electric corner modes in continuum quantum gauge theory with matter
summary: Subregions in gauge theories give rise to edge modes and corner charges supported on their boundaries. While this is well-established classically and in quantum lattice gauge theories, the fate of corner modes remains poorly understood in continuum quantum field theories owing to their distributional nature. In this paper, we revisit this challenge and propose a new corner operator for a regional Cauchy slice algebra generated by local gauge-invariant observables of scalar QED in Minkowski spacetime. The corner mode is given by the longitudinal electric field sourced by the matter outside the subregion and thus constitutes a centre for the regional algebra. Our main goal is to show that there exists a perturbative GNS state on this algebra that quantises this mode. Pulling back the Fock vacuum to the slice, we construct this state by renormalising the divergences arising from the lack of temporal smearing. We clarify that the inclusion of the new centre mode necessitates a further renormalisation on the corner of the region, thereby physically distinguishing it and breaking the translation invariance of the state. Our work shows how the requirements of locality, renormalisability, and positivity together put strong constraints on the existence of a continuum quantum field theory which supports corner modes as genuine quantum operators. We finish with comments about the von Neumann completion of the regional algebra, as well as possible physical interpretations of the renormalised vacuum state.

title: Finite-Depth Null Capture and Mass-History Sensitivity in Vaidya Spacetime
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 3 tables; ancillary code and numerical data included
summary: We formulate a finite-depth endpoint map for past-directed null rays in dynamical black-hole spacetimes, retaining an unresolved label when no terminal is reached before a prescribed optical depth. For regular transverse terminal hits, common-flow, transversality, and separation hypotheses make the regular decision sets open and the endpoint label locally constant. In Schwarzschild spacetime, the resulting finite-depth capture circle converges to the standard critical circle as $\exp[-L/(3M)]$ when the cutoff is measured in static-observer optical depth. We then apply the construction to ingoing Vaidya spacetime. Two $C^4$ accretion profiles that coincide on a neighborhood of the observation event, and therefore have identical local mass and metric jets there, nevertheless produce distinct finite-depth critical angles. For the baseline protocol, $Δ_{\mathrm{hist}}α_{45}=0.0819062ε-0.0231767ε^2+O(ε^3)$. A backward adjoint gives an explicit causal kernel representing the first-order response to the mass history. The kernel is broad, peaks away from the photon-sphere dwell region, and changes between finite backgrounds even where their instantaneous masses agree. The quadratic coefficient is independently confirmed by centered nonlinear solutions and Richardson extrapolation. These results separate instability-controlled cutoff convergence from globally transported mass-history sensitivity.

title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
summary: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant. Our results show that the observational tension encountered in the minimal quartic double-well model need not extend to topological inflation in a minimal multi-natural axion potential.

title: New Effects in Multifield Cosmology Coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet Term
summary: We study the rapid-turn regime of multifield cosmology coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. We derive the corresponding modified relations between the inflationary Hubble and potential slow-roll parameters, in the two-field case. These relations show that including the Gauss-Bonnet coupling broadens the possibilities for realizing rapid turn inflation and for satisfying the swampland conjectures. We also derive a consistency condition relating the scalar field-space metric to the scalar potential and the Gauss-Bonnet coupling, which two-field slow-roll and rapid-turn inflationary solutions have to satisfy. Finally, we find general conditions under which phantom-like behavior is possible in multifield dark energy models coupled to the Gauss-Bonnet term. Notably, although we do not consider a direct interaction between dark matter and dark energy, dark matter is crucial for the occurrence of a phantom regime.

title: The JWST/PASSAGE Survey: Metallicity Radial Gradients in Emission-Line Galaxy Pairs at Cosmic Noon with NIRISS
comment: 26 pages, 9 figures. Submitted to ApJ; revised following the referee's comments
summary: Using JWST/NIRISS slitless spectroscopy from the PASSAGE program, we analyze 17 spectroscopically confirmed emission-line galaxies in candidate interacting systems at $z \sim 1.7$--$3.2$. These galaxies span stellar masses of $7.3 \lesssim \log(M_*/M_\odot) \lesssim 10.4$ and global gas-phase metallicities of $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H}) \sim 7.6$--$8.7$. From spatially resolved emission-line maps, we measure radial metallicity gradients separately for each galaxy, finding values from approximately $-0.2$ to $+0.45$ dex kpc$^{-1}$. The mean metallicity gradients in bins of stellar mass and redshift are consistent with previous measurements, and their scatter is not significantly different from that of the heterogeneous literature compilation in either the metallicity-gradient--stellar-mass or metallicity-gradient--redshift relation. We find tentative evidence for an anti-correlation between the metallicity gradient and the metallicity offset from the mass--metallicity relation, with a best-fit slope of $-0.30 \pm 0.06$, possibly reflecting interaction-driven variations in star formation and chemical enrichment. Galaxies in pairs with comparable component masses tend to exhibit positive metallicity gradients, whereas galaxies in unequal-mass pairs tend to exhibit negative gradients; neither trend is statistically significant in the present sample. Overall, our results reveal substantial diversity in the metallicity distributions of candidate interacting systems at cosmic noon and provide tentative evidence that galaxy interactions may influence the redistribution of gas and metals.

title: Gravitational Memory from AdS States in the Flat-Space Limit
summary: We study linearized gravitational reconstruction in global AdS$_4$ with dynamical scalar matter, building on vacuum Einstein perturbations with fixed boundary metric and nontrivial normalizable data. External scalar sources prepare an excited state and modify the holographic Ward identities, while subsequent evolution can proceed without boundary driving. Separating the bulk matter-sourced response from vacuum perturbations, we derive an electric quadrupole master equation with the matter-dependent corrections required by the Einstein constraints. We also verify that a cylindrical boundary integral reproduces the Regge--Wheeler master field mode by mode, without identifying it with the full global Fefferman--Graham reconstruction. For weakly interacting scalars that become massless in the flat-space limit, we extract the Bondi shear and news from retarded gravitational evolution. The resulting supertranslation memory agrees numerically with the outgoing energy redistribution and the quadrupole moment of the boundary work. In the ordered flat-space limit, later boundary controls leave the first event's waveform unchanged, despite cancelling residual gravitational modes at finite AdS radius.

title: Neutrino Oscillation in a Static Dihole Geometry
summary: We investigate neutrino flavor oscillations in the static equal-mass Majumdar-Papapetrou dihole geometry, restricting the propagation to the symmetry plane. Within the null approximation, we derive the leading contribution to the neutrino phase and numerically evaluate the geodesic integrals. For two neutrino flavors, interference between different trajectories introduces a dependence on the individual neutrino masses and on the neutrino mass ordering for nonmaximal mixing. We analyze the transition probability in different spacetime configurations possessing two light rings, a merged light ring (critical configuration), and no light rings in the equatorial plane. In the weak-lensing regime, the transition probability generally increases with the black holes' individual masses, while variations in the half-separation produce no qualitative change in the transition probability. In stronger-lensing configurations, variations in both the mass and half-separation modify the heights and positions of the extrema, with no monotonic increase or decrease in the transition probability. For the critical and no-light-ring configurations studied, we identify three zero-winding trajectories connecting the source and detector, including one passing near the symmetry axis. The probability remains oscillatory, and its oscillatory pattern depends strongly on the neutrino energy.

title: Two-loop integrals for $t\bar{t}γ$ production at hadron colliders in the leading-colour approximation
comment: 32 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables, ancillary files at https://zenodo.org/records/23799374
summary: We complete the calculation of the two-loop Feynman integrals required for the next-to-next-to-leading order QCD corrections to on-shell top--antitop production in association with a photon at hadron colliders, in the leading-colour approximation. The same integrals also enter the subleading-colour corrections to top--antitop production in association with a jet. We construct integral bases that satisfy algebraic differential equations. These are largely in canonical form; the exceptions are a few entries, associated with elliptic curves or nested square roots, that depend at most quadratically on the dimensional regulator $ε$. We solve the differential equations in terms of a tailored set of special functions, which will enable the analytic extraction of the two-loop finite remainder. We evaluate these functions by numerically solving the differential equations they satisfy, and show that the resulting routine is fast and stable enough in the physical region for phenomenological applications.

title: From thermogravity to thermocosmology with a running non-conservation scale
summary: Thermogravity offers a novel approach to cosmic acceleration, deriving trace-free gravitational equations and matter non-conservation from thermodynamic processes in spacetime. We extend this framework towards thermocosmology by introducing a running non-conservation scale $L_2(H)$, while restricting non-conservation to cold dark matter. We investigate two prescriptions, namely a Hubble-proportional rate and an inverse-Hubble running model, deriving their cosmological dynamics and effective geometric dark-energy description. The first admits an exact analytical solution and is related to quadratic running-vacuum cosmologies, while the second approaches standard matter dilution at early times and allows reversals in the direction of energy exchange. Interestingly, the reconstructed geometric dark energy can exhibit quintessence-like and phantom-like behavior, including smooth crossings of the phantom divide, without introducing a phantom field or superacceleration. A unified dynamical-system analysis reveals distinct matter-era critical configurations and a continuous family of de Sitter solutions that are transversely attracting under suitable conditions. Confronting both models with Pantheon+ Type Ia supernovae, cosmic chronometers, and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations, we find a mild preference for positive present-day matter non-conservation. The Akaike information criterion slightly favors the thermogravity scenarios, whereas the Bayesian information criterion favors the simpler $Λ$CDM model. Thus, running thermocosmology provides a viable framework for nontrivial effective dark-energy dynamics.

title: Co-evolution of AGN and Host Galaxies across Cosmic Time Using JWST data
summary: Understanding the complex co-evolution of active galactic nuclei (AGN) and their host galaxies across cosmic time remains a fundamental challenge, particularly in identifying how the physical drivers of galaxy diversity evolve from the early Universe to the present day. To understand this, we use a multi-wavelength JWST catalog of 2,709 sources cross-matched from the SMILES and JWST Advanced Deep Extragalactic Survey (JADES) surveys, spanning lookback times from 0.8 to 12.9 Gyr ($0.05 <z <6$). Using Pearson correlation matrix, we find AGN luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{AGN}}$) strongly correlates ($\sim0.8$) with star formation rate (SFR) and dust luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{dust}}$), weakly correlates ($\sim0.5$) with stellar mass ($M_\star$) and anti-correlates ($\sim -0.4$) with star formation history (SFH) duration and stellar age (Age$_\star$). However, the apparent anti-correlation observed between galaxy age and AGN luminosity is driven by cosmic time rather than by a direct physical connection. Using Principal Component Analysis (PCA), we find that galaxy diversity is fundamentally governed by two principal components: AGN and galaxy activity, and stellar age. At higher redshifts, AGN accretion, star formation, and dust emission are tightly synchronized, reflecting gas-rich conditions in the early Universe. In contrast, the present Universe exhibits a clear bimodal structure in host-dominated systems ($f_{\mathrm{AGN}} \leq 0.2$), separating quiescent and star-forming galaxies. Our results demonstrate that AGN luminosity is primarily governed by the host galaxy's current cold-gas supply, of which recent star formation is a close observational tracer, with galaxy mass setting the overall potential. This highlights a co-evolution scenario in which black hole growth and star formation are tightly linked, particularly at early cosmic epochs.

title: Light-Transformed Carrollian OPEs and the Four-Gluon Spectral Bootstrap
summary: Scattering amplitudes of massless particles can be rewritten as correlation functions of light-transformed operators at null infinity, on which the Carrollian symmetries act. We ask how much of the four-gluon tree amplitude is determined by the operator product expansion of these operators. When two gluons become collinear, the exchanged gluon and all of its descendants combine into a single function of the null time of $\mathcal{I}^+$ and angular separations of the pair on the celestial sphere. We show that this function is fixed by the Ward identities, which reduce to Kummer's differential equation, and by the signs of the energies, which select one combination of its two solutions. We then expand the same amplitude in massive two-particle states of the physical scattering channel and find that the collinear data control the expansion at large spin. Each of the two collinear poles of the amplitude determines one of the two infinite sequences of partial-wave coefficients in closed form. Once both poles are imposed, crossing symmetry and the scaling of the correlator in Carroll time fix the tree spectrum uniquely among amplitudes with only the physical collinear poles, up to a single subtraction constant at the collinear boundary.

title: Scattering of massless scalar waves by higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics
summary: We study the scattering of planar massless scalar waves by the family of higher-dimensional regular black holes in general relativity coupled to nonlinear electrodynamics, which unifies the Bardeen and Hayward models in any dimension. The scalar field is a neutral test field that propagates in the bulk, and in the geometric-optics limit, its rays are the null geodesics of the spacetime, so that the unstable circular null geodesics of the background geometry control the scattering. We combine the classical scattering of null geodesics, the glory approximation, which we generalize to $D$ dimensions, and the partial-wave analysis in $D=5,6,7$. We show that at a fixed frequency, the wave cross section diverges in the forward direction as $θ^{-4}$ in any dimension, with a coefficient fixed by the mass, while the steeper classical law $θ^{-(D-2)^{2}/(D-3)}$ appears only at larger angles and higher frequencies. The charge parameter decreases the critical and the glory impact parameters and widens the glory fringes, and in higher dimensions, the glory pattern has fewer and wider fringes and a weaker backward intensity. For the matched configurations studied here, backward intensity and low-frequency absorption provide the clearest differences, while the intermediate-to-high-frequency spectra are close.

title: Hints of self-interacting dark matter from strong gravitational lensing
comment: Companion paper to JWST Lensed Quasar Dark Matter Survey V; submitted to PRL, comments welcome
summary: An analysis of 29 quadruply imaged quasars hints at dark matter halo densities consistent with gravothermal core collapse, a key prediction of self-interacting dark matter. We interpret this evidence through elastic Yukawa scattering, combining lensing with upper limits on the cross-section strength from galaxy clusters and Milky Way satellite evaporation. Favored models have dark matter masses of $20$-$80\,{\rm GeV}$, MeV-scale mediators, and Yukawa-potential strengths near $10^{-3}$, yielding cross-sections of $10^2$--$10^4 \, {\rm cm^2\,g^{-1}}$ at $10\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$. Cosmological, direct and indirect detection bounds on MeV-scale mediators motivate a neutrinophilic scalar dilepton that decays invisibly without Higgs mixing. These results demonstrate how inferences on core collapse constrain dark sector physics.

title: Topological Multi-Natural Inflation
summary: We investigate topological inflation in minimal multi-natural inflation, in which the axion potential consists of two cosine terms. Focusing on the high-scale regime, we perform a systematic parameter scan for representative ratios of the two periods and identify regions consistent with current constraints on the scalar spectral index and tensor-to-scalar ratio, including those from the Atacama Cosmology Telescope. The interplay of the two harmonics allows departures from the quartic hilltop limit and accommodates the higher spectral index favored by recent cosmological data combinations. We characterize the hilltop and near-inflection-point branches and analyze the associated vacuum structure and domain-wall properties. We also discuss a symmetry-breaking origin of the required domain walls when the inflaton is the angular component of a complex scalar field. We identify regions in which the observational constraints and the adopted criteria for topological inflation are simultaneously satisfied, including regions with a sub-Planckian axion decay constant.
